column9: Besides "inside and outside", in writing it can follow a number to mean "around" (三十歲內外); in speech people say 左右. 內 is made of 入 (to enter) and 冂 (house): it first meant to bring into the house.

column3: Describes what comes from outside a place or group: 外来人口 (migrants), 外来语 (loanwords), 外来物种 (invasive species). 来 began as a picture of wheat, and was borrowed for "to come" very early.
column6: Wàilái de yóukè yuè lái yuè duō.
column7: More and more outside visitors are coming.
column9: Describes what comes from outside a place or group: 外來人口 (migrants), 外來語 (loanwords), 外來物種 (invasive species). 來 began as a picture of wheat, and was borrowed for "to come" very early.

column3: Used for a physical edge and for a figurative one: 悬崖的边缘, but also 边缘人 (someone on the margins) and 在崩溃的边缘 (on the verge of collapse).
column4: 公司已经走到破产的边缘。
column5: 公司已經走到破產的邊緣。
column6: Gōngsī yǐjīng zǒu dào pòchǎn de biānyuán.
column7: The company has come to the brink of bankruptcy.
column9: Used for a physical edge and for a figurative one: 懸崖的邊緣, but also 邊緣人 (someone on the margins) and 在崩潰的邊緣 (on the verge of collapse).

column3: Takes its object directly: 远离城市, 远离危险. Also a warning or slogan to stay away from something harmful: 远离毒品.
column6: Háizimen yīnggāi yuǎnlí wēixiǎn.
column7: Children should stay away from danger.
column9: Takes its object directly: 遠離城市, 遠離危險. Also a warning or slogan to stay away from something harmful: 遠離毒品.

column3: A doubled 远 for emphasis. Before a verb it adds "from a distance": 远远地看. Before 超过 or 不如 it means "by far": 远远超过.
column6: Tā yuǎnyuǎn de kànzhe wǒmen.
column7: He watched us from far away.
column9: A doubled 遠 for emphasis. Before a verb it adds "from a distance": 遠遠地看. Before 超過 or 不如 it means "by far": 遠遠超過.

column3: Said of meeting or talking in person, as against by phone or online: 面对面交流. It comes before the verb, often with 地. 面 began as a picture of a face with the eye drawn oversized.
column4: 我们面对面地谈一谈吧。
column5: 我們面對面地談一談吧。
column6: Wǒmen miànduìmiàn de tán yī tán ba.
column7: Let's talk face to face.
column9: Said of meeting or talking in person, as against by phone or online: 面對面交流. It comes before the verb, often with 地. 面 began as a picture of a face with the eye drawn oversized.

column3: Two uses: "to face" a direction (房子面向大海) and "to be aimed at" an audience (面向全国, 面向学生).
column6: Zhè mén kè miànxiàng suǒyǒu xuésheng.
column7: This course is open to all students.
column9: Two uses: "to face" a direction (房子面向大海) and "to be aimed at" an audience (面向全國, 面向學生).

column3: A written word for tomorrow, found in news and set phrases such as 明日之星 (a rising star). In speech people say 明天. 明 puts the sun 日 and the moon 月 together: the sun just rising while the moon has not yet set, which is dawn.
column4: 他是我们公司的明日之星。
column5: 他是我們公司的明日之星。
column6: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de míngrì zhī xīng.
column7: He is the rising star of our company.
column9: A written word for tomorrow, found in news and set phrases such as 明日之星 (a rising star). In speech people say 明天. 明 puts the sun 日 and the moon 月 together: the sun just rising while the moon has not yet set, which is dawn.

column3: In the last or next few days, depending on the verb's time: a past verb means "lately", a future one means "soon" (近日上映, coming soon). Written style.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng jìnrì shàngyìng.
column7: This film opens in the next few days.
column9: In the last or next few days, depending on the verb's time: a past verb means "lately", a future one means "soon" (近日上映, coming soon). Written style.

column3: Used before a verb to mean "around the clock": 日夜工作, 日夜思念. 日日夜夜 is the stronger, more emotional form.
column6: Yīshēng rìyè zhàogù zhe bìngrén.
column7: The doctor looks after the patient day and night.
column9: Used before a verb to mean "around the clock": 日夜工作, 日夜思念. 日日夜夜 is the stronger, more emotional form.

column3: Means years gone by in general, not one particular year, so it is the usual basis for comparison: 比往年冷, 与往年相比. 年 first meant a harvest, and grain 禾 is its meaning part.
column6: Jīnnián de xuě bǐ wǎngnián duō.
column7: There is more snow this year than in past years.
column9: Means years gone by in general, not one particular year, so it is the usual basis for comparison: 比往年冷, 與往年相比. 年 first meant a harvest, and grain 禾 is its meaning part.

column3: A time of year, usually with its weather or customs: 清明时节, 收获的时节. It is a written, scenic word; for "time" in general use 时候.
column6: Zhèng shì táohuā shèngkāi de shíjié.
column7: It is just the season when the peach blossoms are in bloom.
column9: A time of year, usually with its weather or customs: 清明時節, 收獲的時節. It is a written, scenic word; for "time" in general use 時候.

column3: Says a state or habit has ended ("no longer") or a decision is final ("never again"): 他不再抽烟了. 再也不 is the stronger form. 不 began as a picture of a flower's calyx; the meaning "no" spread back to it from 否, which was made with it.
column6: Tā bùzài chōuyān le.
column7: He doesn't smoke anymore.
column9: Says a state or habit has ended ("no longer") or a decision is final ("never again"): 他不再抽菸了. 再也不 is the stronger form. 不 began as a picture of a flower's calyx; the meaning "no" spread back to it from 否, which was made with it.

column3: Describes a stance or habit that has never changed: 一贯的态度, 一贯守时. It works for good and bad traits alike.
column6: Tā yīguàn hěn shǒushí.
column7: He has always been punctual.
column9: Describes a stance or habit that has never changed: 一貫的態度, 一貫守時. It works for good and bad traits alike.

column3: Everywhere on the ground: things lie about or grow all over a place (遍地都是). 遍地开花 is also figurative for something spreading everywhere.
column4: 秋天，遍地都是金黄的落叶。
column5: 秋天，遍地都是金黃的落葉。
column6: Qiūtiān, biàndì dōu shì jīnhuáng de luòyè.
column7: In autumn, golden leaves cover the ground everywhere.
column9: Everywhere on the ground: things lie about or grow all over a place (遍地都是). 遍地開花 is also figurative for something spreading everywhere.

column3: Often an adjective before a noun: 常规检查 (routine checkup), 常规武器 (conventional weapons). 打破常规 means to break with convention.
column4: 医生给他做了常规检查。
column5: 醫生給他做了常規檢查。
column6: Yīshēng gěi tā zuò le chángguī jiǎnchá.
column7: The doctor gave him a routine checkup.
column9: Often an adjective before a noun: 常規檢查 (routine checkup), 常規武器 (conventional weapons). 打破常規 means to break with convention.

column3: The place comes first and what covers it after: 天空布满乌云, 脸上布满皱纹. Often used for something unwelcome or striking. 布 is both cloth and "to spread out".
column6: Tiānkōng bùmǎn le wūyún.
column7: The sky is covered with dark clouds.
column9: The place comes first and what covers it after: 天空布滿烏雲, 臉上布滿皺紋. Often used for something unwelcome or striking. 布 is both cloth and "to spread out".

column3: Says a condition lasts all year or for many years, not that something happens often: 常年积雪, 常年在外. 常 first meant a skirt-like garment, and was borrowed for "long-lasting; frequently".
column4: 这座山的山顶常年积雪。
column5: 這座山的山頂常年積雪。
column6: Zhè zuò shān de shāndǐng chángnián jīxuě.
column7: The top of this mountain has snow all year round.
column9: Says a condition lasts all year or for many years, not that something happens often: 常年積雪, 常年在外. 常 first meant a skirt-like garment, and was borrowed for "long-lasting; frequently".

column3: A public holiday whose traditions are eating 粽子 (sticky rice in leaves) and racing dragon boats (赛龙舟). 午 began as a picture of a pestle, now written 杵.
column4: 端午节我们一起包粽子。
column5: 端午節我們一起包粽子。
column6: Duānwǔjié wǒmen yīqǐ bāo zòngzi.
column7: On Dragon Boat Festival we make zongzi together.
column9: A public holiday whose traditions are eating 粽子 (sticky rice in leaves) and racing dragon boats (賽龍舟). 午 began as a picture of a pestle, now written 杵.

column3: The usual verb is 扫墓: families visit and tidy their ancestors' graves and leave offerings. It is a public holiday.
column4: 清明节我们全家去扫墓。
column5: 清明節我們全家去掃墓。
column6: Qīngmíngjié wǒmen quánjiā qù sǎomù.
column7: On Qingming our whole family goes to sweep the graves.
column9: The usual verb is 掃墓: families visit and tidy their ancestors' graves and leave offerings. It is a public holiday.

column3: Often shortened to 圣诞 in greetings and compounds: 圣诞快乐 (Merry Christmas), 圣诞树 (Christmas tree), 圣诞老人 (Santa Claus).
column4: 圣诞节快到了，商店里挂满了彩灯。
column5: 聖誕節快到了，商店裡掛滿了彩燈。
column6: Shèngdànjié kuài dào le, shāngdiàn lǐ guà mǎn le cǎidēng.
column7: Christmas is near, and the stores are hung with colored lights.
column9: Often shortened to 聖誕 in greetings and compounds: 聖誕快樂 (Merry Christmas), 聖誕樹 (Christmas tree), 聖誕老人 (Santa Claus).

column3: Covers festivals (节日) and days off (假日) together, so it names all the days off in the year. 法定节假日 are the holidays set by law.
column4: 节假日期间，景点里人很多。
column5: 節假日期間，景點裡人很多。
column6: Jiéjiàrì qījiān, jǐngdiǎn lǐ rén hěn duō.
column7: During the holidays, the sights are crowded.
column9: Covers festivals (節日) and days off (假日) together, so it names all the days off in the year. 法定節假日 are the holidays set by law.

column3: Often the week-long national breaks, as in 国庆长假. 休长假 is to take a long leave. Here 长 is read cháng, not zhǎng. 长 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.
column4: 国庆长假我打算去旅行。
column5: 國慶長假我打算去旅行。
column6: Guóqìng chángjià wǒ dǎsuàn qù lǚxíng.
column7: I plan to travel during the National Day holiday.
column9: Often the week-long national breaks, as in 國慶長假. 休長假 is to take a long leave. Here 長 is read cháng, not zhǎng. 長 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.

column3: The usual word for fireworks: 放烟花 (set them off), 看烟花. In old Yuan-era drama it could also mean a prostitute.
column4: 今晚广场上有烟花表演。
column5: 今晚廣場上有煙花表演。
column6: Jīnwǎn guǎngchǎng shàng yǒu yānhuā biǎoyǎn.
column7: There is a fireworks show on the square tonight.
column9: The usual word for fireworks: 放煙花 (set them off), 看煙花. In old Yuan-era drama it could also mean a prostitute.

column3: Said of numbers, dates, words and omens people hope for: 8 is a 吉利 number, and 说吉利话 is to say lucky things at New Year. 利 shows grain 禾 being cut with a knife 刀.
column4: 他们选了一个吉利的日子结婚。
column5: 他們選了一個吉利的日子結婚。
column6: Tāmen xuǎn le yī gè jílì de rìzi jiéhūn.
column7: They chose a lucky day for the wedding.
column9: Said of numbers, dates, words and omens people hope for: 8 is a 吉利 number, and 說吉利話 is to say lucky things at New Year. 利 shows grain 禾 being cut with a knife 刀.

column3: More ceremonial than 吉利, seen in blessings (吉祥如意) and in 吉祥物, a mascot that is meant to bring good luck.
column4: 这只熊猫是大会的吉祥物。
column5: 這隻熊貓是大會的吉祥物。
column6: Zhè zhī xióngmāo shì dàhuì de jíxiáng wù.
column7: This panda is the mascot of the event.
column9: More ceremonial than 吉利, seen in blessings (吉祥如意) and in 吉祥物, a mascot that is meant to bring good luck.

column3: A warm, somewhat formal "I wish that..." with the person and the wish after it: 祝愿你一切顺利. Plain 祝 is lighter and more common. 祝 pictures a man kneeling with his mouth open (兄) beside an altar (示).
column6: Zhùyuàn nǐ yīqiè shùnlì.
column7: I wish you every success.
column9: A warm, somewhat formal "I wish that..." with the person and the wish after it: 祝願你一切順利. Plain 祝 is lighter and more common. 祝 pictures a man kneeling with his mouth open (兄) beside an altar (示).

column3: Giving a gift for an occasion or to someone you owe. With a boss or an official it can hint at buying favor.
column4: 过年的时候，大家会给亲戚送礼。
column5: 過年的時候，大家會給親戚送禮。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, dàjiā huì gěi qīnqi sònglǐ.
column7: At New Year, people give gifts to their relatives.
column9: Giving a gift for an occasion or to someone you owe. With a boss or an official it can hint at buying favor.

column3: A king's wife. A woman who rules in her own right is a 女王, not a 王后.
column6: Wánghòu zuò zài guówáng de shēnbiān.
column7: The queen sits beside the king.
column9: A king's wife. A woman who rules in her own right is a 女王, not a 王后.

column3: Appears in 佛教 (Buddhism), 佛像 (Buddha statue) and 阿弥陀佛. In 仿佛 it is read fú, a different word. One scholar thinks 佛 was likely borrowed from Iranian, ultimately from Sanskrit "buddha".
column6: Sìmiào lǐ yǒu yī zūn dà fó.
column7: There is a great Buddha statue in the temple.
column9: Appears in 佛教 (Buddhism), 佛像 (Buddha statue) and 阿彌陀佛. In 仿佛 it is read fú, a different word. One scholar thinks 佛 was likely borrowed from Iranian, ultimately from Sanskrit "buddha".

column3: Mostly the last part of a temple's name, as in 少林寺; 清真寺 is a mosque. In speech the general word is 寺庙. 寺 was first about grasping and holding (hence the hand 又); 持 is the character for that original word.
column4: 这座寺有一千多年的历史。
column5: 這座寺有一千多年的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò sì yǒu yī qiān duō nián de lìshǐ.
column7: This temple has over a thousand years of history.
column9: Mostly the last part of a temple's name, as in 少林寺; 清真寺 is a mosque. In speech the general word is 寺廟. 寺 was first about grasping and holding (hence the hand 又); 持 is the character for that original word.

column3: Mostly found in compounds: 坟墓, 墓地 (cemetery), 墓碑 (headstone). 扫墓 is to visit and tidy a grave.
column4: 他每年都去给祖父扫墓。
column5: 他每年都去給祖父掃墓。
column6: Tā měi nián dōu qù gěi zǔfù sǎo mù.
column7: Every year he goes to tend his grandfather's grave.
column9: Mostly found in compounds: 墳墓, 墓地 (cemetery), 墓碑 (headstone). 掃墓 is to visit and tidy a grave.

column3: A palace, as in 故宫 (the Forbidden City) and 宫殿. It also names grand public halls: 少年宫 is a children's after-school activity center.
column4: 他们参观了北京的故宫。
column5: 他們參觀了北京的故宮。
column6: Tāmen cānguān le Běijīng de gù gōng.
column7: They visited the Palace Museum in Beijing.
column9: A palace, as in 故宮 (the Forbidden City) and 宮殿. It also names grand public halls: 少年宮 is a children's after-school activity center.

column3: The tall structure in compounds such as 宝塔 (pagoda), 灯塔 (lighthouse), 电视塔 and 金字塔 (a pyramid). 塔 was borrowed from a Middle Indo-Aryan language; compare Pali thūpa and Sanskrit stūpa.
column4: 山顶上有一座古老的塔。
column5: 山頂上有一座古老的塔。
column6: Shāndǐng shàng yǒu yī zuò gǔlǎo de tǎ.
column7: There is an old pagoda on the hilltop.
column9: The tall structure in compounds such as 寶塔 (pagoda), 燈塔 (lighthouse), 電視塔 and 金字塔 (a pyramid). 塔 was borrowed from a Middle Indo-Aryan language; compare Pali thūpa and Sanskrit stūpa.

column3: Only the words of a song, not the tune. Credits split the work into 作词 (lyrics) and 作曲 (music).
column6: Zhè shǒu gē de gēcí hěn gǎnrén.
column7: The lyrics of this song are very moving.
column9: Only the words of a song, not the tune. Credits split the work into 作詞 (lyrics) and 作曲 (music).

column3: You sing it (唱国歌) or an orchestra plays it (奏国歌), and people stand for it. 升国旗、奏国歌 is the flag-raising set phrase.
column4: 比赛前，大家一起唱国歌。
column5: 比賽前，大家一起唱國歌。
column6: Bǐsài qián, dàjiā yīqǐ chàng guógē.
column7: Before the match, everyone sings the national anthem together.
column9: You sing it (唱國歌) or an orchestra plays it (奏國歌), and people stand for it. 升國旗、奏國歌 is the flag-raising set phrase.

column3: Folk songs of a region or ethnic group, passed down among ordinary people: 陕北民歌, 蒙古民歌. Not pop songs (流行歌曲). 民 in its oldest forms looks like an eye pierced by a cross-shaped sharp implement.
column6: Tā huì chàng hěn duō míngē.
column7: She can sing many folk songs.
column9: Folk songs of a region or ethnic group, passed down among ordinary people: 陝北民歌, 蒙古民歌. Not pop songs (流行歌曲). 民 in its oldest forms looks like an eye pierced by a cross-shaped sharp implement.

column3: A piece of music, usually without singing, played by an instrument or orchestra: 钢琴乐曲. Here 乐 is read yuè (music), not lè (happy). 乐 comes from a character that pictured strings on a piece of wood, a wooden instrument; 曲 pictures a bent object.
column6: Zhè shǒu yuèqǔ yóu gāngqín yǎnzòu.
column7: This piece is played on the piano.
column9: A piece of music, usually without singing, played by an instrument or orchestra: 鋼琴樂曲. Here 樂 is read yuè (music), not lè (happy). 樂 pictured strings on a piece of wood, a wooden instrument; 曲 pictures a bent object.

column3: To play music before an audience or at a ceremony: 奏国歌, 演奏, 伴奏 (accompany), 独奏 (solo). It is rarely used alone for casual playing; that is 弹 or 拉. 奏 may show two hands holding an object, perhaps a musical instrument used in a sacrificial ritual.
column6: Yuèduì zhèngzài zòu guógē.
column7: The band is playing the national anthem.
column9: To play music before an audience or at a ceremony: 奏國歌, 演奏, 伴奏 (accompany), 獨奏 (solo). It is rarely used alone for casual playing; that is 彈 or 拉. 奏 may show two hands holding an object, perhaps a musical instrument used in a sacrificial ritual.

column3: The umbrella term for all Chinese opera, such as 京剧 and 昆曲, with their singing, speech, acting and martial arts. 戏 has 戈 (a halberd) and originally referred to the wing or flank of an army.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan tīng xìqǔ.
column7: Since childhood she has liked listening to Chinese opera.
column9: The umbrella term for all Chinese opera, such as 京劇 and 崑曲, with their singing, speech, acting and martial arts. 戲 has 戈 (a halberd) and originally referred to the wing or flank of an army.

column3: Rhythm in music, and also pace in life or work: 生活节奏, 加快节奏, 节奏很快.
column6: Chéngshì shēnghuó de jiézòu hěn kuài.
column7: The pace of city life is fast.
column9: Rhythm in music, and also pace in life or work: 生活節奏, 加快節奏, 節奏很快.

column3: The sound of laughter, often with a measure: 一阵笑声, 笑声不断. 声 after a verb gives its sound: 哭声, 歌声, 掌声, 雨声.
column6: Jiàoshì lǐ chuánlái yī zhèn xiàoshēng.
column7: A burst of laughter came from the classroom.
column9: The sound of laughter, often with a measure: 一陣笑聲, 笑聲不斷. 聲 after a verb gives its sound: 哭聲, 歌聲, 掌聲, 雨聲.

column3: In daily use an entertainer such as a singer, actor or comedian, not a fine artist (艺术家, 画家). 民间艺人 are folk craftspeople.
column4: 这位艺人在台上又唱又跳。
column5: 這位藝人在台上又唱又跳。
column6: Zhè wèi yìrén zài tái shàng yòu chàng yòu tiào.
column7: This performer sings and dances on stage.
column9: In daily use an entertainer such as a singer, actor or comedian, not a fine artist (藝術家, 畫家). 民間藝人 are folk craftspeople.

column3: 星 after a field names its famous performers: 影星 for film, 歌星 for singing, 球星 for ball sports. 星 was first written as 晶, twinkling stars, and the 生 was added later.
column4: 她是一位很有名的影星。
column5: 她是一位很有名的影星。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi hěn yǒumíng de yǐngxīng.
column7: She is a very famous film star.
column9: 星 after a field names its famous performers: 影星 for film, 歌星 for singing, 球星 for ball sports. 星 was first written as 晶, twinkling stars, and the 生 was added later.

column3: 迷 after a hobby names its fans: 影迷 for films, 球迷 for ball games, 歌迷 for a singer's followers.
column4: 我爸爸是个老影迷，家里有很多老电影。
column5: 我爸爸是個老影迷，家裡有很多老電影。
column6: Wǒ bàba shì ge lǎo yǐngmí, jiālǐ yǒu hěn duō lǎo diànyǐng.
column7: My dad is an old movie buff, and we have lots of old films at home.
column9: 迷 after a hobby names its fans: 影迷 for films, 球迷 for ball games, 歌迷 for a singer's followers.

column3: A somewhat formal word for painting as an art: 绘画作品, 绘画比赛. For simply drawing something, people say 画画. The ancient forms of 画 hold a brush 聿, not a field.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan huìhuà.
column7: She has loved painting since she was little.
column9: A somewhat formal word for painting as an art: 繪畫作品, 繪畫比賽. For simply drawing something, people say 畫畫. The ancient forms of 畫 hold a brush 聿, not a field.

column3: The general word for animation. 动画片 is a cartoon film or series, and 动漫 covers animation and comics together.
column6: Zhè bù dònghuà hěn yǒuyìsi.
column7: This animated film is very interesting.
column9: The general word for animation. 動畫片 is a cartoon film or series, and 動漫 covers animation and comics together.

column3: Covers a short film at a festival as well as a clip of a few minutes shared online. A full-length film is 长片.
column4: 他拍了一部关于家乡的短片。
column5: 他拍了一部關於家鄉的短片。
column6: Tā pāi le yī bù guānyú jiāxiāng de duǎnpiàn.
column7: He made a short film about his hometown.
column9: Covers a short film at a festival as well as a clip of a few minutes shared online. A full-length film is 長片.

column3: The play, film or show is what is staged: 新戏上演 or 上演一出戏. It is also used for events that play out like a drama, as in 上演一场好戏.
column4: 这部话剧下个月在北京上演。
column5: 這部話劇下個月在北京上演。
column6: Zhè bù huàjù xià ge yuè zài Běijīng shàngyǎn.
column7: This stage play opens in Beijing next month.
column9: The play, film or show is what is staged: 新戲上演 or 上演一出戲. It is also used for events that play out like a drama, as in 上演一場好戲.

column3: It ends kinds of show (电视剧, 京剧, 话剧) and begins places (剧场, 剧院); in speech 剧 alone means a TV series: 这部剧很好看, 追剧.
column6: Wǒ wǎnshang xǐhuan zhuī jù.
column7: In the evening I like to binge TV series.
column9: It ends kinds of show (電視劇, 京劇, 話劇) and begins places (劇場, 劇院); in speech 劇 alone means a TV series: 這部劇很好看, 追劇.

column3: A scene in a film, play or game, or the setting where something happens. In business and tech, 使用场景 means the situation in which a product is used. 景 originally meant sunlight.
column4: 这部电影的最后一个场景让我很感动。
column5: 這部電影的最後一個場景讓我很感動。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng de zuìhòu yī gè chǎngjǐng ràng wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
column7: The last scene of this movie moved me deeply.
column9: A scene in a film, play or game, or the setting where something happens. In business and tech, 使用場景 means the situation in which a product is used. 景 originally meant sunlight.

column3: To take part in an exhibition or trade fair as an exhibitor: 参展商 is an exhibitor and 参展作品 the works on show. A visitor just 参观, visits.
column4: 我们公司今年也会在博览会上参展。
column5: 我們公司今年也會在博覽會上參展。
column6: Wǒmen gōngsī jīnnián yě huì zài bólǎnhuì shang cānzhǎn.
column7: Our company will also exhibit at the expo this year.
column9: To take part in an exhibition or trade fair as an exhibitor: 參展商 is an exhibitor and 參展作品 the works on show. A visitor just 參觀, visits.

column3: The round before the final: 进入半决赛 is to reach the semifinals. The quarterfinal is 四分之一决赛. 半 is 八, to divide, with 牛, a cow: a cow cut into two halves.
column4: 中国队顺利进入了半决赛。
column5: 中國隊順利進入了半決賽。
column6: Zhōngguó duì shùnlì jìnrù le bànjuésài.
column7: The Chinese team made it into the semifinals.
column9: The round before the final: 進入半決賽 is to reach the semifinals. The quarterfinal is 四分之一決賽. 半 is 八, to divide, with 牛, a cow: a cow cut into two halves.

column3: A big organized contest, often open to the public and not only in sport: 歌唱大赛, 摄影大赛, 编程大赛. A single match is 比赛.
column4: 她参加了全国歌唱大赛。
column5: 她參加了全國歌唱大賽。
column6: Tā cānjiā le quánguó gēchàng dàsài.
column7: She entered the national singing contest.
column9: A big organized contest, often open to the public and not only in sport: 歌唱大賽, 攝影大賽, 編程大賽. A single match is 比賽.

column3: A league, in which teams play each other through a whole season, as in 英超联赛. A knockout tournament is 杯赛.
column4: 这支球队连续三年赢得联赛冠军。
column5: 這支球隊連續三年贏得聯賽冠軍。
column6: Zhè zhī qiúduì liánxù sān nián yíngdé liánsài guànjūn.
column7: This team has won the league title three years in a row.
column9: A league, in which teams play each other through a whole season, as in 英超聯賽. A knockout tournament is 杯賽.

column3: A verb: to enter a contest. 参赛者 and 参赛选手 are the competitors, 参赛作品 the entries. Its partner for exhibitions is 参展. 参 first named the Three Stars group, and one reading sees a person looking up at the shining stars.
column4: 一共有五十支队伍参赛。
column5: 一共有五十支隊伍參賽。
column6: Yīgòng yǒu wǔshí zhī duìwu cānsài.
column7: Fifty teams in all are entering.
column9: A verb: to enter a contest. 參賽者 and 參賽選手 are the competitors, 參賽作品 the entries. Its partner for exhibitions is 參展. 參 first named the Three Stars group, and one reading sees a person looking up at the shining stars.

column3: Mostly it sits inside compounds: 比赛, 决赛, 赛场, 赛跑, 赛车. Spoken, it is also a casual verb, as in 咱们赛一赛, let's race.
column4: 我们来赛一赛，看谁跑得快。
column5: 我們來賽一賽，看誰跑得快。
column6: Wǒmen lái sài yī sài, kàn shéi pǎo de kuài.
column7: Let's have a race and see who runs faster.
column9: Mostly it sits inside compounds: 比賽, 決賽, 賽場, 賽跑, 賽車. Spoken, it is also a casual verb, as in 咱們賽一賽, let's race.

column3: The place where a contest is held, such as the track, court or pitch. 赛场上 is also used for what happens during the match.
column4: 运动员们在赛场上全力以赴。
column5: 運動員們在賽場上全力以赴。
column6: Yùndòngyuánmen zài sàichǎng shàng quánlì yǐfù.
column7: The athletes gave it their all on the field.
column9: The place where a contest is held, such as the track, court or pitch. 賽場上 is also used for what happens during the match.

column3: Singles in tennis, badminton and table tennis. The short forms are 男单 and 女单; doubles is 双打, and 混双 is mixed doubles.
column4: 她在女子单打比赛中夺冠。
column5: 她在女子單打比賽中奪冠。
column6: Tā zài nǚzǐ dāndǎ bǐsài zhōng duóguàn.
column7: She won the women's singles title.
column9: Singles in tennis, badminton and table tennis. The short forms are 男單 and 女單; doubles is 雙打, and 混雙 is mixed doubles.

column3: Doubles in racket sports. A team of two is a pair of 搭档, partners, and mixed doubles is 混双. 双 is simply 又 written twice.
column6: Wǒmen liǎ yīqǐ dǎ shuāngdǎ ba.
column7: Let's play doubles together.
column9: Doubles in racket sports. A team of two is a pair of 搭檔, partners, and mixed doubles is 混雙. 雙 is simply 又 written twice.

column3: Short for 田赛 (field events such as jumping and throwing) and 径赛 (track events). You see it in 田径队, 田径比赛 and 田径运动会.
column4: 她是学校田径队的队员。
column5: 她是學校田徑隊的隊員。
column6: Tā shì xuéxiào tiánjìng duì de duìyuán.
column7: She is a member of the school track and field team.
column9: Short for 田賽 (field events such as jumping and throwing) and 徑賽 (track events). You see it in 田徑隊, 田徑比賽 and 田徑運動會.

column3: Distance running as a sport or training: 长跑比赛, 长跑运动员. A sprint is 短跑, and easy jogging for fitness is 慢跑. 长 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.
column4: 每天早上他都坚持长跑。
column5: 每天早上他都堅持長跑。
column6: Měitiān zǎoshang tā dōu jiānchí chángpǎo.
column7: He sticks to distance running every morning.
column9: Distance running as a sport or training: 長跑比賽, 長跑運動員. A sprint is 短跑, and easy jogging for fitness is 慢跑. 長 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.

column3: Diving into water from a board or platform, as an Olympic sport. Diving with a tank to look underwater is 潜水, a different word.
column4: 她跳水的动作非常漂亮。
column5: 她跳水的動作非常漂亮。
column6: Tā tiàoshuǐ de dòngzuò fēicháng piàoliang.
column7: Her dives are very graceful.
column9: Diving into water from a board or platform, as an Olympic sport. Diving with a tank to look underwater is 潛水, a different word.

column3: The medals go 金牌, 银牌, 铜牌. You win one with 获得, 夺得 or 拿到, and 铜牌 in sport means third place.
column4: 他在比赛中拿到了一块铜牌。
column5: 他在比賽中拿到了一塊銅牌。
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng nádào le yī kuài tóngpái.
column7: He won a bronze medal in the competition.
column9: The medals go 金牌, 銀牌, 銅牌. You win one with 獲得, 奪得 or 拿到, and 銅牌 in sport means third place.

column3: One word for the racket in tennis and badminton and the paddle in table tennis: 网球拍, 羽毛球拍, 乒乓球拍. The 拍 is also a verb, to pat or clap, as in 拍手.
column4: 我的球拍断了，得买新的。
column5: 我的球拍斷了，得買新的。
column6: Wǒ de qiúpāi duàn le, děi mǎi xīn de.
column7: My racket broke, so I need to buy a new one.
column9: One word for the racket in tennis and badminton and the paddle in table tennis: 網球拍, 羽毛球拍, 乒乓球拍. The 拍 is also a verb, to pat or clap, as in 拍手.

column3: A famous player in a ball sport, most often football or basketball. The same 星 after a field gives 影星 and 歌星, and the fans are 球迷.
column4: 他是全国最有名的球星之一。
column5: 他是全國最有名的球星之一。
column6: Tā shì quánguó zuì yǒumíng de qiúxīng zhī yī.
column7: He is one of the most famous sports stars in the country.
column9: A famous player in a ball sport, most often football or basketball. The same 星 after a field gives 影星 and 歌星, and the fans are 球迷.

column3: A children's ball to bounce and throw. 踢皮球 is a set phrase for passing the buck: each office kicks the problem to the next. A ball was first written 球, with 毛, hair, and 球 became the usual form later.
column4: 孩子们在院子里拍皮球。
column5: 孩子們在院子裡拍皮球。
column6: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ pāi píqiú.
column7: The children are bouncing a ball in the yard.
column9: A children's ball to bounce and throw. 踢皮球 is a set phrase for passing the buck: each office kicks the problem to the next. A ball was first written 毬, with 毛, hair, and 球 became the usual form later.

column3: In sport it is a foul. The verb 犯 goes with other wrongs too: 犯错 to make a mistake, 犯罪 to commit a crime. 规 comes from an older form that began as a picture of a measuring compass; the husband and see parts were put in later.
column6: Tā yīnwèi fànguī bèi fá xià chǎng.
column7: He was sent off for a foul.
column9: In sport it is a foul. The verb 犯 goes with other wrongs too: 犯錯 to make a mistake, 犯罪 to commit a crime. 規 comes from an older form that began as a picture of a measuring compass; the husband and see parts were put in later.

column3: A chart ranking songs, books, films or sales, as in 畅销书排行榜. A 榜 is a posted list: 榜首 is the top spot and 上榜 is to make the list. Here 行 is read háng.
column4: 这首歌登上了音乐排行榜第一名。
column5: 這首歌登上了音樂排行榜第一名。
column6: Zhè shǒu gē dēngshàng le yīnyuè páihángbǎng dì yī míng.
column7: This song reached number one on the music chart.
column9: A chart ranking songs, books, films or sales, as in 暢銷書排行榜. A 榜 is a posted list: 榜首 is the top spot and 上榜 is to make the list. Here 行 is read háng.

column3: Attack in war and the offense in sport. The opposite is 防守, defense, and teams 发起进攻, launch an attack.
column4: 球队开场就发起了进攻。
column5: 球隊開場就發起了進攻。
column6: Qiúduì kāichǎng jiù fāqǐ le jìngōng.
column7: The team went on the attack right from the start.
column9: Attack in war and the offense in sport. The opposite is 防守, defense, and teams 發起進攻, launch an attack.

column3: 打 is the verb for most games and ball sports: 打球, 打麻将, 打游戏. 玩 also works for casual play. A friendly pastime for families and friends.
column4: 周末他们常常一起打牌。
column5: 週末他們常常一起打牌。
column6: Zhōumò tāmen chángcháng yīqǐ dǎpái.
column7: On weekends they often play cards together.
column9: 打 is the verb for most games and ball sports: 打球, 打麻將, 打遊戲. 玩 also works for casual play. A friendly pastime for families and friends.

column3: 机 ends the names of machines: 游戏机, 打印机, 录音机. A console at home is 游戏机, and an arcade machine is 街机. Simplified 游 stands for both swimming and 遊, roaming and traveling.
column4: 他的游戏机是去年生日收到的礼物。
column5: 他的遊戲機是去年生日收到的禮物。
column6: Tā de yóuxìjī shì qùnián shēngrì shōudào de lǐwù.
column7: His game console was a birthday gift from last year.
column9: 機 ends the names of machines: 遊戲機, 打印機, 錄音機. A console at home is 遊戲機, and an arcade machine is 街機.

column3: A formal word used by schools, companies and communities: 文娱活动, 文娱节目. In everyday talk people say 娱乐. 文 went from a pattern or tattoo, to written characters, to literature and then to refined and cultured.
column4: 学校每周都有文娱活动。
column5: 學校每週都有文娛活動。
column6: Xuéxiào měi zhōu dōu yǒu wényú huódòng.
column7: The school has recreational activities every week.
column9: A formal word used by schools, companies and communities: 文娛活動, 文娛節目. In everyday talk people say 娛樂. 文 went from a pattern or tattoo, to written characters, to literature and then to refined and cultured.

column3: It praises: strong energy and enthusiasm for something. 充满激情 is full of passion, and 激情四射 is radiating it. Used for speeches, songs, teams and young people.
column6: Tā jiǎnghuà chōngmǎn jīqíng.
column7: He speaks with great passion.
column9: It praises: strong energy and enthusiasm for something. 充滿激情 is full of passion, and 激情四射 is radiating it. Used for speeches, songs, teams and young people.

column3: Two everyday uses: to send someone off, as in 打发他走, and to pass time, as in 打发时间, often when bored. The 发 is neutral tone.
column4: 我在咖啡店看书打发时间。
column5: 我在咖啡店看書打發時間。
column6: Wǒ zài kāfēidiàn kàn shū dǎfa shíjiān.
column7: I pass the time reading at a café.
column9: Two everyday uses: to send someone off, as in 打發他走, and to pass time, as in 打發時間, often when bored. The 發 is neutral tone.

column3: A colloquial word for feeling great or satisfied: 太爽了, 吃得很爽. Its opposite is 不爽, to feel annoyed or unhappy.
column6: Xǐ wán zǎo, wǒ juéde tèbié shuǎng.
column7: After my shower I feel really refreshed.
column9: A colloquial word for feeling great or satisfied: 太爽了, 吃得很爽. Its opposite is 不爽, to feel annoyed or unhappy.

column3: Being connected and talking: 通话时间 is the length of a call, 通话中 means the line is busy, and 保持通话 is stay on the line. Dialing is 打电话.
column6: Wǒmen tōnghuà le shí fēnzhōng.
column7: We talked on the phone for ten minutes.
column9: Being connected and talking: 通話時間 is the length of a call, 通話中 means the line is busy, and 保持通話 is stay on the line. Dialing is 打電話.

column3: A service hotline: 客服热线, 服务热线, 举报热线, or 热线电话. It is the public number to call for help, complaints or advice.
column4: 有问题请拨打客服热线。
column5: 有問題請撥打客服熱線。
column6: Yǒu wèntí qǐng bōdǎ kèfú rèxiàn.
column7: If you have a problem, please call the customer service hotline.
column9: A service hotline: 客服熱線, 服務熱線, 舉報熱線, or 熱線電話. It is the public number to call for help, complaints or advice.

column3: A single page on the web, while 网站 is a whole site. You 打开网页, and 网页版 is the browser version of an app. 页 began as a picture of a person's head, and later came to mean a sheet or page.
column6: Zhège wǎngyè dǎ bù kāi le.
column7: This web page won't open.
column9: A single page on the web, while 網站 is a whole site. You 打開網頁, and 網頁版 is the browser version of an app. 頁 began as a picture of a person's head, and later came to mean a sheet or page.

column3: Mostly used before a noun: 多媒体教室 (a classroom with computer and projector), 多媒体设备, 多媒体课件. A little dated as a tech word now. 多 pictures two pieces of meat, and one scholar suggests that meant many because meat was scarce.
column4: 教室里有一套多媒体设备。
column5: 教室裡有一套多媒體設備。
column6: Jiàoshì lǐ yǒu yī tào duōméitǐ shèbèi.
column7: The classroom has a set of multimedia equipment.
column9: Mostly used before a noun: 多媒體教室 (a classroom with computer and projector), 多媒體設備, 多媒體課件. A little dated as a tech word now. 多 pictures two pieces of meat, and one scholar suggests that meant many because meat was scarce.

column3: A technical word for moving data, signals, power or fuel along a line: 数据传输, 传输速度, 无线传输. For passing a message between people use 传达.
column4: 网络太慢，文件传输了很久。
column5: 網路太慢，檔案傳輸了很久。
column6: Wǎngluò tài màn, wénjiàn chuánshū le hěn jiǔ.
column7: The network was slow, so the file took a long time to transfer.
column9: A technical word for moving data, signals, power or fuel along a line: 數據傳輸, 傳輸速度, 無線傳輸. For passing a message between people use 傳達.

column3: Most often an online platform: 社交平台, 电商平台, 直播平台. The platform at a train station is a different word, 站台 or 月台.
column4: 这个平台上有很多免费课程。
column5: 這個平臺上有很多免費課程。
column6: Zhège píngtái shàng yǒu hěn duō miǎnfèi kèchéng.
column7: This platform has many free courses.
column9: Most often an online platform: 社交平臺, 電商平臺, 直播平臺. The platform at a train station is a different word, 站臺 or 月臺.

column3: The formal phrasing on notices and in announcements, with a phone number or line as its object: 拨打热线. In chat people simply say 打电话.
column4: 遇到问题请拨打客服电话。
column5: 遇到問題請撥打客服電話。
column6: Yùdào wèntí qǐng bōdǎ kèfú diànhuà.
column7: If you run into a problem, please call customer service.
column9: The formal phrasing on notices and in announcements, with a phone number or line as its object: 撥打熱線. In chat people simply say 打電話.

column3: Any display: phone, computer or TV, as in 手机屏幕 and 触摸屏幕. The big cinema screen is usually 银幕. On the mainland 屏幕 is the standard word; Taiwan usually says 萤幕.
column6: Shǒujī píngmù shuāihuài le.
column7: The phone screen is broken from a fall.
column9: Any display: phone, computer or TV, as in 手機屏幕 and 觸摸屏幕. The big cinema screen is usually 銀幕. On the mainland 屏幕 is the standard word; Taiwan usually says 螢幕.

column3: Both the verb and the footage: 监控录像 is surveillance footage and 看录像 is to watch a replay. On the mainland 录像 is the usual word; Taiwan says 录影.
column6: Jǐngchá chákàn le jiānkòng lùxiàng.
column7: The police looked at the surveillance footage.
column9: Both the verb and the footage: 監控錄像 is surveillance footage and 看錄像 is to watch a replay. On the mainland 錄像 is the usual word; Taiwan says 錄影.

column3: Found in trade terms: 音像制品 (recordings sold as products), 音像店, 音像出版社. Tapes, CDs and DVDs belong to it, so it feels a bit dated.
column4: 这家音像店卖很多老唱片。
column5: 這家音像店賣很多老唱片。
column6: Zhè jiā yīnxiàng diàn mài hěn duō lǎo chàngpiàn.
column7: This shop sells lots of old records.
column9: Found in trade terms: 音像製品 (recordings sold as products), 音像店, 音像出版社. Tapes, CDs and DVDs belong to it, so it feels a bit dated.

column3: Now mainly the old tape recorder. Recording today is just 录音, and a small voice recorder is a 录音笔. Like 游戏机, it ends in the machine word 机.
column4: 爷爷还留着一台旧录音机。
column5: 爺爺還留著一台舊錄音機。
column6: Yéye hái liúzhe yī tái jiù lùyīnjī.
column7: Grandpa still keeps an old tape recorder.
column9: Now mainly the old tape recorder. Recording today is just 錄音, and a small voice recorder is a 錄音筆. Like 遊戲機, it ends in the machine word 機.

column3: How loud the sound is: 调大音量 turns it up, 调小音量 turns it down, and 音量键 is the volume button. 声音 is the sound itself. 音 is 言 with one short extra stroke inside the mouth, probably suggesting a muffled sound.
column6: Qǐng bǎ yīnliàng tiáo xiǎo yīdiǎn.
column7: Please turn the volume down a little.
column9: How loud the sound is: 調大音量 turns it up, 調小音量 turns it down, and 音量鍵 is the volume button. 聲音 is the sound itself. 音 is 言 with one short extra stroke inside the mouth, probably suggesting a muffled sound.

column3: The noise something makes, such as a bang, a rattle or a knock: 发出响声, 一阵响声. It is not for voices or music; for sound in general use 声音.
column4: 楼上突然传来一阵响声。
column5: 樓上突然傳來一陣響聲。
column6: Lóushàng tūrán chuánlái yī zhèn xiǎngshēng.
column7: A sudden noise came from upstairs.
column9: The noise something makes, such as a bang, a rattle or a knock: 發出響聲, 一陣響聲. It is not for voices or music; for sound in general use 聲音.

column3: 打印 prints out from a computer, while 印刷 is mass printing of books and papers. In Taiwan the printer is usually 印表机 and to print is 列印. 印 is drawn as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person.
column6: Dǎyìnjī lǐ méiyǒu zhǐ le.
column7: The printer is out of paper.
column9: 打印 prints out from a computer, while 印刷 is mass printing of books and papers. In Taiwan the printer is usually 印表機 and to print is 列印. 印 is drawn as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person.

column3: A formal word for the press: newspapers and magazines together, as in 报刊杂志. The 刊 also ends 期刊 (journal) and 周刊 (weekly magazine).
column6: Túshūguǎn lǐ yǒu hěn duō bàokān.
column7: The library has many newspapers and magazines.
column9: A formal word for the press: newspapers and magazines together, as in 報刊雜誌. The 刊 also ends 期刊 (journal) and 週刊 (weekly magazine).

column3: Often the media as an industry or institution: 传媒公司, 传媒大学, 传媒行业. For a particular outlet or the news media, 媒体 is the common word.
column4: 他在一家传媒公司工作。
column5: 他在一家傳媒公司工作。
column6: Tā zài yī jiā chuánméi gōngsī gōngzuò.
column7: He works at a media company.
column9: Often the media as an industry or institution: 傳媒公司, 傳媒大學, 傳媒行業. For a particular outlet or the news media, 媒體 is the common word.

column3: Official language: authorities 通报 a case or result to the public, as in 疫情通报. 通报批评 is a public notice of criticism.
column4: 警方通报了案件的最新情况。
column5: 警方通報了案件的最新情況。
column6: Jǐngfāng tōngbào le ànjiàn de zuìxīn qíngkuàng.
column7: The police announced the latest developments in the case.
column9: Official language: authorities 通報 a case or result to the public, as in 疫情通報. 通報批評 is a public notice of criticism.

column3: A named, recurring slot in a paper, a website or a broadcast schedule, such as 体育栏目 for sports. A show that airs weekly under a fixed name is a 栏目 too.
column6: Wǒ měitiān dōu kàn zhège lánmù.
column7: I watch this program every day.
column9: A named, recurring slot in a paper, a website or a broadcast schedule, such as 體育欄目 for sports. A show that airs weekly under a fixed name is a 欄目 too.

column3: The leaflet packed with a product, a medicine or a device. You look at it with 看说明书, and 使用说明书 is the full name for the how-to-use kind.
column6: Yòng zhīqián qǐng xiān kàn shuōmíngshū.
column7: Please read the instructions before using it.
column9: The leaflet packed with a product, a medicine or a device. You look at it with 看說明書, and 使用說明書 is the full name for the how-to-use kind.

column3: Mostly live commentary on a match or a documentary, given by a 解说员, and also a guide’s explaining talk at a museum or exhibit.
column4: 这场比赛的解说很精彩。
column5: 這場比賽的解說很精彩。
column6: Zhè chǎng bǐsài de jiěshuō hěn jīngcǎi.
column7: The commentary for this match is excellent.
column9: Mostly live commentary on a match or a documentary, given by a 解說員, and also a guide’s explaining talk at a museum or exhibit.

column3: Besides a hot spot, it is a topic everyone is talking about (热点新闻, 热点话题), and the Wi-Fi hotspot on a phone.
column4: 这是今天最大的热点新闻。
column5: 這是今天最大的熱點新聞。
column6: Zhè shì jīntiān zuì dà de rèdiǎn xīnwén.
column7: This is the biggest hot news story today.
column9: Besides a hot spot, it is a topic everyone is talking about (熱點新聞, 熱點話題), and the Wi-Fi hotspot on a phone.

column3: Very often figurative: the center of attention, as in 成为焦点 or 争论的焦点. 焦 was first the name of a kind of bird; the fire part came from a mistaken change of 小 during the Warring States period.
column4: 他的发言成了大家关注的焦点。
column5: 他的發言成了大家關注的焦點。
column6: Tā de fāyán chéng le dàjiā guānzhù de jiāodiǎn.
column7: His speech became the focus of everyone’s attention.
column9: Very often figurative: the center of attention, as in 成為焦點 or 爭論的焦點. 焦 was first the name of a kind of bird; the fire part came from a mistaken change of 小 during the Warring States period.

column3: Usually what comes out of a place or a source: 传出笑声 (laughter drifts out), 传出消息 (word gets out).
column6: Fángjiān lǐ chuánchū le yīnyuè shēng.
column7: Music was coming from the room.
column9: Usually what comes out of a place or a source: 傳出笑聲 (laughter drifts out), 傳出消息 (word gets out).

column3: Mostly figurative: the route by which goods or information reach you, as in 销售渠道 (sales channels), 正规渠道 (official channels) and 沟通渠道.
column4: 你是通过什么渠道知道的？
column5: 你是通過什麼渠道知道的？
column6: Nǐ shì tōngguò shénme qúdào zhīdào de?
column7: How did you find out about it?
column9: Mostly figurative: the route by which goods or information reach you, as in 銷售渠道 (sales channels), 正規渠道 (official channels) and 溝通渠道.

column3: A language name is the country’s short name plus 语: 法国 gives 法语, 英国 gives 英语. You speak it with 说, as in 说法语.
column6: Tā huì shuō Fǎyǔ hé Yīngyǔ.
column7: She can speak French and English.
column9: A language name is the country’s short name plus 語: 法國 gives 法語, 英國 gives 英語. You speak it with 說, as in 說法語.

column3: 日 here is the short name for Japan. Language names take 语 (说日语), while 日文 leans toward the writing.
column6: Wǒ zài xué Rìyǔ.
column7: I am learning Japanese.
column9: 日 here is the short name for Japan. Language names take 語 (說日語), while 日文 leans toward the writing.

column3: 西班牙 only imitates the sound of the country’s name, so its three characters carry no meaning here. For short, people say 西语.
column4: 她的西班牙语说得很流利。
column5: 她的西班牙語說得很流利。
column6: Tā de Xībānyáyǔ shuō de hěn liúlì.
column7: Her Spanish is very fluent.
column9: 西班牙 only imitates the sound of the country’s name, so its three characters carry no meaning here. For short, people say 西語.

column3: A set phrase for muttering aloud to yourself, usually with 在 or 一边: 他在自言自语. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and pointing at your nose is one folk explanation for “oneself”.
column4: 他一边走路，一边自言自语。
column5: 他一邊走路，一邊自言自語。
column6: Tā yībiān zǒulù, yībiān zìyánzìyǔ.
column7: He talked to himself as he walked.
column9: A set phrase for muttering aloud to yourself, usually with 在 or 一邊: 他在自言自語. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and pointing at your nose is one folk explanation for “oneself”.

column3: Often an official or public answer to a question, request or criticism (公开回应, 积极回应). It is a noun too: 没有得到回应.
column4: 公司还没有回应这件事。
column5: 公司還沒有回應這件事。
column6: Gōngsī hái méiyǒu huíyìng zhè jiàn shì.
column7: The company has not yet responded to this matter.
column9: Often an official or public answer to a question, request or criticism (公開回應, 積極回應). It is a noun too: 沒有得到回應.

column3: A rumor passed along by word of mouth, usually introduced as 有传言说…. What the rumor says may well be untrue.
column6: Yǒu chuányán shuō tā yào cízhí.
column7: There is a rumor that he is going to resign.
column9: A rumor passed along by word of mouth, usually introduced as 有傳言說…. What the rumor says may well be untrue.

column3: The public’s reaction to a film, book, policy or event. It usually pairs with 引起 or 产生 and with 强烈, 热烈 or 很大: 引起强烈反响.
column4: 这部电影在国内引起了很大的反响。
column5: 這部電影在國內引起了很大的反響。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng zài guónèi yǐnqǐ le hěn dà de fǎnxiǎng.
column7: This film caused a big stir at home.
column9: The public’s reaction to a film, book, policy or event. It usually pairs with 引起 or 產生 and with 強烈, 熱烈 or 很大: 引起強烈反響.

column3: Introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said, followed by a comma. 也就是说 is a very common variant.
column4: 这就是说，我们得重新开始。
column5: 這就是說，我們得重新開始。
column6: Zhèjiùshìshuō, wǒmen děi chóngxīn kāishǐ.
column7: That is to say, we have to start over.
column9: Introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said, followed by a comma. 也就是說 is a very common variant.

column3: Opens a frank remark, often a mild disagreement. Its full form 说句实话 means the same. A comma follows.
column4: 说实话，我不太喜欢这个颜色。
column5: 說實話，我不太喜歡這個顏色。
column6: Shuōshíhuà, wǒ bù tài xǐhuan zhège yánsè.
column7: To be honest, I don’t like this color much.
column9: Opens a frank remark, often a mild disagreement. Its full form 說句實話 means the same. A comma follows.

column3: A noncommittal answer to a question about the future or a judgment call. It works as a whole reply on its own.
column6: Míngtiān huì xià yǔ ma? Hěnnánshuō.
column7: Will it rain tomorrow? Hard to say.
column9: A noncommittal answer to a question about the future or a judgment call. It works as a whole reply on its own.

column3: Sets up a contrast: how things look on the surface, then 其实 or 但是 how they really are. 表 began as an outer garment, a garment 衣 with hair 毛.
column4: 他表面上很平静，其实很紧张。
column5: 他表面上很平靜，其實很緊張。
column6: Tā biǎomiànshang hěn píngjìng, qíshí hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: He looks calm on the surface, but he is really nervous.
column9: Sets up a contrast: how things look on the surface, then 其實 or 但是 how they really are. 表 began as an outer garment, a garment 衣 with hair 毛.

column3: The sentence-final 啊, written 哇 after a syllable ending in u or ao: 你好哇, 快走哇. The "wow" is the same character read wā.
column6: Kuài zǒu wa, yào chídào le!
column7: Hurry up, we'll be late!
column9: The sentence-final 啊, written 哇 after a syllable ending in u or ao: 你好哇, 快走哇. The "wow" is the same character read wā.

column3: A make-up exam for someone who failed or missed the first one: 参加补考, 补考通过.
column4: 他数学没及格，要参加补考。
column5: 他數學沒及格，要參加補考。
column6: Tā shùxué méi jígé, yào cānjiā bǔkǎo.
column7: He failed math and has to take the make-up exam.
column9: A make-up exam for someone who failed or missed the first one: 參加補考, 補考通過.

column3: The room or hall where an exam is held (进考场, 考场纪律). 考 starts a family: 考题 the questions, 考生 the candidate. 考 began as an old man leaning on a cane.
column6: Qǐng zài bā diǎn qián jìnrù kǎochǎng.
column7: Please enter the exam room before eight.
column9: The room or hall where an exam is held (進考場, 考場紀律). 考 starts a family: 考題 the questions, 考生 the candidate. 考 began as an old man leaning on a cane.

column3: A question on an exam paper, or the questions as a set (考题很难). 试题 is a more formal near-synonym.
column4: 这次的考题比我想的容易。
column5: 這次的考題比我想的容易。
column6: Zhè cì de kǎotí bǐ wǒ xiǎng de róngyì.
column7: The questions this time were easier than I thought.
column9: A question on an exam paper, or the questions as a set (考題很難). 試題 is a more formal near-synonym.

column3: To register for a competitive exam or for a place at a school, with the object right after it: 报考大学, 报考研究生. 报名 is simply to sign up.
column6: Tā dǎsuàn bàokǎo Běijīng Dàxué.
column7: She plans to apply to Peking University.
column9: To register for a competitive exam or for a place at a school, with the object right after it: 報考大學, 報考研究生. 報名 is simply to sign up.

column3: The national college entrance exam, taken each June; for many families the biggest exam of a young person’s life.
column6: Tā míngnián yào cānjiā gāokǎo.
column7: He will take the college entrance exam next year.
column9: The national college entrance exam, taken each June; for many families the biggest exam of a young person’s life.

column3: Required, said of a course or a subject: 必修课 is a required course, against 选修课, an elective that students pick for themselves. Each program lists its 必修 courses.
column4: 这门课是所有学生的必修课。
column5: 這門課是所有學生的必修課。
column6: Zhè mén kè shì suǒyǒu xuésheng de bìxiū kè.
column7: This course is required for all students.
column9: Required, said of a course or a subject: 必修課 is a required course, against 選修課, an elective that students pick for themselves. Each program lists its 必修 courses.

column3: To run a school, the job of a founder or an institution rather than a teacher: 办学条件 (a school’s facilities).
column4: 这所大学已经办学一百多年了。
column5: 這所大學已經辦學一百多年了。
column6: Zhè suǒ dàxué yǐjīng bànxué yībǎi duō nián le.
column7: This university has been running for over a hundred years.
column9: To run a school, the job of a founder or an institution rather than a teacher: 辦學條件 (a school’s facilities).

column3: To teach yourself without a teacher or a class. 自学成才 praises someone who became skilled this way. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and pointing at your nose is one folk explanation for “oneself”.
column6: Wǒ shì zìxué Zhōngwén de.
column7: I taught myself Chinese.
column9: To teach yourself without a teacher or a class. 自學成才 praises someone who became skilled this way. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and pointing at your nose is one folk explanation for “oneself”.

column3: Rare on its own: the everyday words are 认识, 知识, 识字 and 识别. Alone it turns up in set phrases such as 一字不识.
column6: Tā yī gè zì yě bù shí.
column7: He does not know a single character.
column9: Rare on its own: the everyday words are 認識, 知識, 識字 and 識別. Alone it turns up in set phrases such as 一字不識.

column3: To be able to read characters, which is literacy: 不识字 is illiterate and 识字量 is how many characters a person knows. 字 first meant to give birth to or nurture; its sense “character” is either a different word or grew out of “to produce”.
column4: 这个孩子三岁就识字了。
column5: 這個孩子三歲就識字了。
column6: Zhège háizi sān suì jiù shízì le.
column7: This child could read characters at three.
column9: To be able to read characters, which is literacy: 不識字 is illiterate and 識字量 is how many characters a person knows. 字 first meant to give birth to or nurture; its sense “character” is either a different word or grew out of “to produce”.

column3: What a teacher does: give a lesson or lecture (给学生讲课). The student’s side is 听课, and 上课 works for both.
column4: 王老师正在给学生讲课。
column5: 王老師正在給學生講課。
column6: Wáng lǎoshī zhèngzài gěi xuésheng jiǎngkè.
column7: Teacher Wang is giving a lesson to the students.
column9: What a teacher does: give a lesson or lecture (給學生講課). The student’s side is 聽課, and 上課 works for both.

column3: The 好 is read hào, “to like”, so this describes a person who loves learning: 好学的孩子. 好 joins a woman 女 and a child 子 because it was good for a woman to have a child, on the common view.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù hěn hàoxué.
column7: He has loved learning since he was little.
column9: The 好 is read hào, “to like”, so this describes a person who loves learning: 好學的孩子. 好 joins a woman 女 and a child 子 because it was good for a woman to have a child, on the common view.

column3: The first level of a series with 中等 and 高等: 初等教育 is primary education, 初等数学 elementary math. 初 is a garment 衤 and a knife 刀: the start of making clothes is cutting the cloth.
column6: Tā zhǐ shòuguò chūděng jiàoyù.
column7: He only had a primary education.
column9: The first level of a series with 中等 and 高等: 初等教育 is primary education, 初等數學 elementary math. 初 is a garment 衤 and a knife 刀: the start of making clothes is cutting the cloth.

column3: The middle level between 初等 and 高等: 中等教育 is secondary education, and 中等身材 means medium build. 等 has bamboo 竹 on top: it refers to the bamboo strips once written on, for example when grading and sorting.
column4: 他是中等身材，不高也不矮。
column5: 他是中等身材，不高也不矮。
column6: Tā shì zhōngděng shēncái, bù gāo yě bù ǎi.
column7: He is of medium build, neither tall nor short.
column9: The middle level between 初等 and 高等: 中等教育 is secondary education, and 中等身材 means medium build. 等 has bamboo 竹 on top: it refers to the bamboo strips once written on, for example when grading and sorting.

column3: The top level of the series: 高等教育 is higher education, 高等学校 colleges and universities, 高等数学 college-level math. 高 began as a picture of a tall building.
column4: 她在北京接受高等教育。
column5: 她在北京接受高等教育。
column6: Tā zài Běijīng jiēshòu gāoděng jiàoyù.
column7: She received a higher education in Beijing.
column9: The top level of the series: 高等教育 is higher education, 高等學校 colleges and universities, 高等數學 college-level math. 高 began as a picture of a tall building.

column3: 部 ends the names of national ministries: 外交部 foreign affairs, 国防部 defense, 教育部 education.
column4: 教育部宣布了新的考试办法。
column5: 教育部宣布了新的考試辦法。
column6: Jiàoyùbù xuānbù le xīn de kǎoshì bànfǎ.
column7: The Ministry of Education announced new exam rules.
column9: 部 ends the names of national ministries: 外交部 foreign affairs, 國防部 defense, 教育部 education.

column3: Ink for a fountain pen or a printer. The black ink used with a brush is 墨汁, and 肚子里有墨水 jokes that someone is educated.
column6: Wǒ de gāngbǐ méiyǒu mòshuǐ le.
column7: My fountain pen is out of ink.
column9: Ink for a fountain pen or a printer. The black ink used with a brush is 墨汁, and 肚子裡有墨水 jokes that someone is educated.

column3: A written draft or script, especially a speech or article to be read out: 念稿子 reading from it, 写稿子 writing it.
column6: Tā názhe gǎozi shàngtái fāyán.
column7: He went on stage and spoke from a script.
column9: A written draft or script, especially a speech or article to be read out: 唸稿子 reading from it, 寫稿子 writing it.

column3: To earn money by working or trading. 挣钱 is a close alternative, and 赚 alone can mean to turn a profit (赚了一笔).
column6: Tā kào kāi cānguǎn zhuànqián.
column7: He makes money by running a restaurant.
column9: To earn money by working or trading. 掙錢 is a close alternative, and 賺 alone can mean to turn a profit (賺了一筆).

column3: Both the act of setting a price and the list price that results (定价过高). 价格 is the price in general.
column4: 这本书的定价是五十元。
column5: 這本書的定價是五十元。
column6: Zhè běn shū de dìngjià shì wǔshí yuán.
column7: The list price of this book is fifty yuan.
column9: Both the act of setting a price and the list price that results (定價過高). 價格 is the price in general.

column3: The price of homes, a constant topic: 房价上涨, 房价下跌. 价 ends many price words, such as 油价 and 物价.
column4: 这个城市的房价越来越高。
column5: 這個城市的房價越來越高。
column6: Zhège chéngshì de fángjià yuè lái yuè gāo.
column7: Housing prices in this city keep getting higher.
column9: The price of homes, a constant topic: 房價上漲, 房價下跌. 價 ends many price words, such as 油價 and 物價.

column3: Rent paid for a home, a shop, a car or equipment. 房租 is rent for housing in particular. 租 has grain 禾 in it because land rent was paid in grain.
column4: 这里的租金每个月三千块。
column5: 這裡的租金每個月三千塊。
column6: Zhèlǐ de zūjīn měi gè yuè sānqiān kuài.
column7: The rent here is three thousand a month.
column9: Rent paid for a home, a shop, a car or equipment. 房租 is rent for housing in particular. 租 has grain 禾 in it because land rent was paid in grain.

column3: A handling fee charged by a bank or agency for going through a procedure. 手续 alone means formalities (办手续), and 费 ends many fee words, such as 学费. The top stroke of 手 is the bent-over middle finger.
column6: Yínháng yào shōu shǒuxùfèi.
column7: The bank charges a handling fee.
column9: A handling fee charged by a bank or agency for going through a procedure. 手續 alone means formalities (辦手續), and 費 ends many fee words, such as 學費. The top stroke of 手 is the bent-over middle finger.

column3: Money for everyday living costs, often what parents send a student or what a person budgets each month. 生 began as a bud 屮 sprouting from the ground 一.
column4: 我每个月的生活费是三千块。
column5: 我每個月的生活費是三千塊。
column6: Wǒ měi gè yuè de shēnghuófèi shì sānqiān kuài.
column7: My living expenses are three thousand a month.
column9: Money for everyday living costs, often what parents send a student or what a person budgets each month. 生 began as a bud 屮 sprouting from the ground 一.

column3: Foreign currency, as at a bank or exchange (外币兑换, 外币账户). 币 comes from a word for silk given as a gift or sacrificed, which is why it has the cloth 巾.
column4: 这家银行可以兑换外币。
column5: 這家銀行可以兌換外幣。
column6: Zhè jiā yínháng kěyǐ duìhuàn wàibì.
column7: This bank can exchange foreign currency.
column9: Foreign currency, as at a bank or exchange (外幣兌換, 外幣帳戶). 幣 comes from a word for silk given as a gift or sacrificed, which is why it has the cloth 巾.

column3: The formal verb for withdrawing money from an account. In speech 取钱 is more common, and the opposite is 存款. 取 shows an ear 耳 and a hand 又: taking the ear of fallen prey, a hunters’ rite.
column6: Wǒ qù yínháng qǔkuǎn.
column7: I am going to the bank to withdraw money.
column9: The formal verb for withdrawing money from an account. In speech 取錢 is more common, and the opposite is 存款. 取 shows an ear 耳 and a hand 又: taking the ear of fallen prey, a hunters’ rite.

column3: The usual mainland word for an ATM; Taiwan says 提款机. 机 ends names of machines: 飞机, 洗衣机, 手机.
column6: Fùjìn yǒu méiyǒu qǔkuǎnjī?
column7: Is there an ATM nearby?
column9: The usual mainland word for an ATM; Taiwan says 提款機. 機 ends names of machines: 飛機, 洗衣機, 手機.

column3: Seldom used alone: it ends words for tickets and vouchers, such as 优惠券 (coupon), 代金券 and 入场券, and also 债券 (bond). The measure word is 张.
column4: 这张券可以免费换一杯咖啡。
column5: 這張券可以免費換一杯咖啡。
column6: Zhè zhāng quàn kěyǐ miǎnfèi huàn yī bēi kāfēi.
column7: This voucher can be traded for a free coffee.
column9: Seldom used alone: it ends words for tickets and vouchers, such as 優惠券 (coupon), 代金券 and 入場券, and also 債券 (bond). The measure word is 張.

column3: Two uses: wealthy, and, before an abstract noun, “full of”: 富有经验, 富有创意, 富有同情心. The second is very common in writing.
column4: 他是一位富有经验的老师。
column5: 他是一位富有經驗的老師。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi fùyǒu jīngyàn de lǎoshī.
column7: He is a teacher rich in experience.
column9: Two uses: wealthy, and, before an abstract noun, “full of”: 富有經驗, 富有創意, 富有同情心. The second is very common in writing.

column3: A bill or the books: 结账 pay the bill, 记账 keep accounts, 算账 settle up, 账号 an account number.
column6: Nǐ bǎ zhè bǐ zhàng jì xiàlái.
column7: Write this bill down.
column9: A bill or the books: 結帳 pay the bill, 記帳 keep accounts, 算帳 settle up, 帳號 an account number.

column3: Usually with a verb: 欠债 owe, 还债 repay, 讨债 collect. 债务 is the formal word for debts.
column6: Tā qiàn le hěn duō zhài.
column7: He is deep in debt.
column9: Usually with a verb: 欠債 owe, 還債 repay, 討債 collect. 債務 is the formal word for debts.

column3: Counts smells, flows and surges: 一股香味, 一股暖流, 一股力量. As a noun it is also a share in a company, as in 股票 and 股东.
column6: Chúfáng lǐ piāolái yī gǔ xiāngwèi.
column7: A whiff of something delicious drifted in from the kitchen.
column9: Counts smells, flows and surges: 一股香味, 一股暖流, 一股力量. As a noun it is also a share in a company, as in 股票 and 股東.

column3: A 大股东 is a major shareholder, and 股东大会 is the shareholders' meeting. 东 also means the host, who sits on the east side of the guest.
column4: 他是这家公司的大股东。
column5: 他是這家公司的大股東。
column6: Tā shì zhè jiā gōngsī de dà gǔdōng.
column7: He is a major shareholder of this company.
column9: A 大股東 is a major shareholder, and 股東大會 is the shareholders' meeting. 東 also means the host, who sits on the east side of the guest.

column3: Colloquial for playing the stock market, often with a speculative, short-term flavor. The same 炒 turns up in 炒房 (flipping houses) and 炒作 (hyping).
column4: 我爸爸退休后喜欢炒股。
column5: 我爸爸退休後喜歡炒股。
column6: Wǒ bàba tuìxiū hòu xǐhuan chǎogǔ.
column7: Since he retired, my dad has enjoyed playing the stock market.
column9: Colloquial for playing the stock market, often with a speculative, short-term flavor. The same 炒 turns up in 炒房 (flipping houses) and 炒作 (hyping).

column3: Usually disapproving: stirring up attention or prices on purpose, for a celebrity, a product or the housing market.
column4: 这家公司靠炒作来提高知名度。
column5: 這家公司靠炒作來提高知名度。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī kào chǎozuò lái tígāo zhīmíngdù.
column7: This company relies on hype to raise its profile.
column9: Usually disapproving: stirring up attention or prices on purpose, for a celebrity, a product or the housing market.

column3: The everyday word for handling your own money: saving, budgeting, investing. It works as a verb (学理财) and in 理财产品, the investment products banks sell.
column4: 年轻人也应该学习理财。
column5: 年輕人也應該學習理財。
column6: Niánqīngrén yě yīnggāi xuéxí lǐcái.
column7: Young people should learn to manage money too.
column9: The everyday word for handling your own money: saving, budgeting, investing. It works as a verb (學理財) and in 理財產品, the investment products banks sell.

column3: Said of money, houses and other assets that gain value; the opposite is 贬值. 升 began as a picture of a dipper, and it is also a unit of dry measure for grain.
column4: 人民币升值了，出国旅游更划算。
column5: 人民幣升值了，出國旅遊更划算。
column6: Rénmínbì shēngzhí le, chūguó lǚyóu gèng huásuàn.
column7: The yuan has risen in value, so traveling abroad is a better deal.
column9: Said of money, houses and other assets that gain value; the opposite is 貶值. 升 began as a picture of a dipper, and it is also a unit of dry measure for grain.

column3: Besides assets gaining value, it means 'value-added': 增值税 is VAT and 增值服务 is a paid extra service. The earth 土 in 增 fits the idea that things grow in the earth.
column4: 这套房子这几年大幅增值。
column5: 這套房子這幾年大幅增值。
column6: Zhè tào fángzi zhè jǐ nián dàfú zēngzhí.
column7: This apartment has gained a lot of value in recent years.
column9: Besides assets gaining value, it means 'value-added': 增值稅 is VAT and 增值服務 is a paid extra service. The earth 土 in 增 fits the idea that things grow in the earth.

column3: Money or firms from abroad: 外资企业 is a foreign-owned company and 外资银行 a foreign bank. The matching word for domestic capital is 内资.
column4: 很多外资企业在上海设有办事处。
column5: 很多外資企業在上海設有辦事處。
column6: Hěn duō wàizī qǐyè zài Shànghǎi shè yǒu bànshìchù.
column7: Many foreign-funded companies have offices in Shanghai.
column9: Money or firms from abroad: 外資企業 is a foreign-owned company and 外資銀行 a foreign bank. The matching word for domestic capital is 內資.

column3: The name customers know a product by. 名牌 is a famous brand, and 品牌 also works as an adjective: 品牌手机 is a name-brand phone, 品牌效应 the pull of a brand.
column4: 这个品牌的手机很受年轻人欢迎。
column5: 這個品牌的手機很受年輕人歡迎。
column6: Zhège pǐnpái de shǒujī hěn shòu niánqīngrén huānyíng.
column7: This brand's phones are popular with young people.
column9: The name customers know a product by. 名牌 is a famous brand, and 品牌 also works as an adjective: 品牌手機 is a name-brand phone, 品牌效應 the pull of a brand.

column3: Top-quality goods or a fine work of art. A 精品店 is a boutique and 精品咖啡 is specialty coffee. 品 ends many words for goods: 成品, 物品, 食品, 商品.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn zhǐ mài jīngpǐn kāfēi.
column7: This shop sells only specialty coffee.
column9: Top-quality goods or a fine work of art. A 精品店 is a boutique and 精品咖啡 is specialty coffee. 品 ends many words for goods: 成品, 物品, 食品, 商品.

column3: The finished goods at the end of production; the stage before is 半成品, half-finished. Cooks also use it for ready-made food.
column4: 这些成品要先检查，再装箱。
column5: 這些成品要先檢查，再裝箱。
column6: Zhèxiē chéngpǐn yào xiān jiǎnchá, zài zhuāngxiāng.
column7: These finished products must be checked first, then packed.
column9: The finished goods at the end of production; the stage before is 半成品, half-finished. Cooks also use it for ready-made food.

column3: Items people own or carry, as on signs and notices: 个人物品 (personal belongings), 贵重物品 (valuables), 违禁物品 (prohibited items). 品 is a 口 written three times, standing for various objects.
column6: Qǐng dài hǎo nín de gèrén wùpǐn.
column7: Please take your personal belongings with you.
column9: Items people own or carry, as on signs and notices: 個人物品 (personal belongings), 貴重物品 (valuables), 違禁物品 (prohibited items). 品 is a 口 written three times, standing for various objects.

column3: Made in the country in question, which on the mainland means made in China: 国产车 is a domestic car, 国产电影 a domestic film. In 国, jade 玉 replaces the 或 inside the box.
column4: 这款国产手机的质量很好。
column5: 這款國產手機的品質很好。
column6: Zhè kuǎn guóchǎn shǒujī de zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
column7: The quality of this domestic phone is very good.
column9: Made in the country in question, which on the mainland means made in China: 國產車 is a domestic car, 國產電影 a domestic film.

column3: A grade or tier of goods: 高档 high-end, 中档 mid-range, 低档 low-end. Also files, as in 档案, and a time slot, as in 档期 (a film's run). In Taiwan it is usually read dǎng.
column4: 这种手表分高、中、低三档。
column5: 這種手錶分高、中、低三檔。
column6: Zhè zhǒng shǒubiǎo fēn gāo, zhōng, dī sān dàng.
column7: This kind of watch comes in three grades: high, middle and low.
column9: A grade or tier of goods: 高檔 high-end, 中檔 mid-range, 低檔 low-end. Also files, as in 檔案, and a time slot, as in 檔期 (a film's run). In Taiwan it is usually read dǎng.

column3: Ends many words for stuff: 材料 (materials), 原料 (raw material), 饮料 (drink), 调料 (seasoning). The 'expect' sense is in 料想 and 出乎意料 (beyond all expectation). 料 puts rice and a dipper together, for measuring.
column6: Tā zǎo jiù liào dào huì zhèyàng.
column7: He saw long ago that it would turn out this way.
column9: Ends many words for stuff: 材料 (materials), 原料 (raw material), 飲料 (drink), 調料 (seasoning). The 'expect' sense is in 料想 and 出乎意料 (beyond all expectation). 料 puts rice and a dipper together, for measuring.

column3: Marks something set aside for one use or group, on signs and notices: 专用车道 (dedicated lane), 残疾人专用 (for disabled people only). The user or purpose comes before it.
column4: 这条车道是公交车专用的。
column5: 這條車道是公交車專用的。
column6: Zhè tiáo chēdào shì gōngjiāochē zhuānyòng de.
column7: This lane is for buses only.
column9: Marks something set aside for one use or group, on signs and notices: 專用車道 (dedicated lane), 殘疾人專用 (for disabled people only). The user or purpose comes before it.

column3: Stronger than 新: brand new, as in ads and launches (全新升级). 全 shows a whole piece of jade. 新 began as the word for firewood, with 斤 for chopping wood, and was later borrowed for "new".
column4: 公司推出了全新的手机。
column5: 公司推出了全新的手機。
column6: Gōngsī tuīchū le quánxīn de shǒujī.
column7: The company has launched an all-new phone.
column9: Stronger than 新: brand new, as in ads and launches (全新升級). 全 shows a whole piece of jade. 新 began as the word for firewood, with 斤 for chopping wood, and was later borrowed for "new".

column3: Praises how something looks and is made: 精美的礼盒, 包装精美, 图案精美. It is for objects, not for people. 美 began as a picture of a person (大) wearing a headdress of feathers or ram's horn.
column4: 她收到了一份精美的礼物。
column5: 她收到了一份精美的禮物。
column6: Tā shōudào le yī fèn jīngměi de lǐwù.
column7: She received an exquisite gift.
column9: Praises how something looks and is made: 精美的禮盒, 包裝精美, 圖案精美. It is for objects, not for people. 美 began as a picture of a person (大) wearing a headdress of feathers or ram's horn.

column3: The switch you press, the on/off toggle in an app, and the act of opening and closing. 电源开关 is the power switch and 总开关 the main switch.
column6: Qǐng àn yī xià zhège kāiguān.
column7: Please press this switch.
column9: The switch you press, the on/off toggle in an app, and the act of opening and closing. 電源開關 is the power switch and 總開關 the main switch.

column3: In electrical talk it is the wiring or circuit; in transport it is the route of a bus, subway or rail line: 地铁线路, 线路图 (route map).
column6: Zhè tiáo xiànlù jīngguò shì zhōngxīn.
column7: This route passes through the city center.
column9: In electrical talk it is the wiring or circuit; in transport it is the route of a bus, subway or rail line: 地鐵線路, 線路圖 (route map).

column3: For machines, vehicles and systems that stop working properly, never for people: 发生故障, 排除故障 (fix a fault), 电梯故障. Software bugs count too.
column6: Diàntī chūxiàn gùzhàng le.
column7: The elevator has broken down.
column9: For machines, vehicles and systems that stop working properly, never for people: 發生故障, 排除故障 (fix a fault), 電梯故障. Software bugs count too.

column3: For computers it means the specs (电脑配置) or setting up (配置文件, a config file). For staff and resources it means allocating: 资源配置.
column6: Zhè tái diànnǎo de pèizhì hěn gāo.
column7: This computer has high-end specs.
column9: For computers it means the specs (電腦配置) or setting up (配置文件, a config file). For staff and resources it means allocating: 資源配置.

column3: Gear, especially for sport, the military and games (游戏装备 is in-game gear). It is also a verb: to equip someone or something. The long form of 备 shows a person carrying a quiver, ready for action.
column4: 他买了一套新的登山装备。
column5: 他買了一套新的登山裝備。
column6: Tā mǎi le yī tào xīn de dēngshān zhuāngbèi.
column7: He bought a new set of mountaineering gear.
column9: Gear, especially for sport, the military and games (遊戲裝備 is in-game gear). It is also a verb: to equip someone or something. The long form of 備 shows a person carrying a quiver, ready for action.

column3: In apps and navigation it is locating a position (定位功能). In business it is positioning: 市场定位 is market positioning, and 把…定位为… means to define something as.
column6: Shǒujī de dìngwèi gōngnéng hěn zhǔn.
column7: The phone's location feature is very accurate.
column9: In apps and navigation it is locating a position (定位功能). In business it is positioning: 市場定位 is market positioning, and 把…定位為… means to define something as.

column3: Ongoing watching with instruments, in news and official reports: 空气质量监测, 实时监测 (real-time monitoring). 监 pictures a person looking into a container, and is the original form of 鉴, mirror.
column4: 环保部门每天监测空气质量。
column5: 環保部門每天監測空氣品質。
column6: Huánbǎo bùmén měi tiān jiāncè kōngqì zhìliàng.
column7: The environmental agency monitors air quality every day.
column9: Ongoing watching with instruments, in news and official reports: 空氣質量監測, 實時監測 (real-time monitoring). 監 pictures a person looking into a container, and is the original form of 鑑, mirror.

column3: Working out a precise value by measuring, as in labs: 测定含量, 测定结果. Where 监测 keeps watching, 测定 ends in a figure.
column4: 科学家测定了这种水的酸碱度。
column5: 科學家測定了這種水的酸鹼度。
column6: Kēxuéjiā cèdìng le zhè zhǒng shuǐ de suānjiǎndù.
column7: The scientist measured the acidity of this water.
column9: Working out a precise value by measuring, as in labs: 測定含量, 測定結果. Where 監測 keeps watching, 測定 ends in a figure.

column3: Two uses: to operate machinery by hand (操纵飞机), and to pull strings behind the scenes (操纵市场, 操纵舆论), which is negative.
column6: Tā zài mùhòu cāozòng zhe yīqiè.
column7: He pulls all the strings behind the scenes.
column9: Two uses: to operate machinery by hand (操縱飛機), and to pull strings behind the scenes (操縱市場, 操縱輿論), which is negative.

column3: After a verb it means doing something properly, with some effort: 打扮一番, 研究一番. Before a noun: 一番话, 一番心意. 翻一番 means to double.
column6: Tā zǐxì dǎban le yīfān.
column7: He dressed up carefully.
column9: After a verb it means doing something properly, with some effort: 打扮一番, 研究一番. Before a noun: 一番話, 一番心意. 翻一番 means to double.

column3: An adverb meaning 'together', a bit more written than 一起: 一道去, 一道走. In 一道菜 or 一道题 it is just 一 plus the measure word 道.
column6: Tāmen yīdào zǒuchū le jiàoshì.
column7: They walked out of the classroom together.
column9: An adverb meaning 'together', a bit more written than 一起: 一道去, 一道走. In 一道菜 or 一道題 it is just 一 plus the measure word 道.

column3: After a leader's name it means that person and the party with them: 市长一行 is the mayor and his delegation, common in news. Read yī xíng; 一行 as 'one row' is yī háng.
column6: Shìzhǎng yīxíng cānguān le gōngchǎng.
column7: The mayor and his party visited the factory.
column9: After a leader's name it means that person and the party with them: 市長一行 is the mayor and his delegation, common in news. Read yī xíng; 一行 as 'one row' is yī háng.

column3: Square meters, often shortened to 平 in speech (八十平). In Taiwan the meter is usually 公尺, as in 平方公尺, and homes are measured in 坪.
column4: 这套房子有八十平方米。
column5: 這套房子有八十平方米。
column6: Zhè tào fángzi yǒu bāshí píngfāngmǐ.
column7: This apartment is eighty square meters.
column9: Square meters, often shortened to 平 in speech (八十平). In Taiwan the meter is usually 公尺, as in 平方公尺, and homes are measured in 坪.

column3: The simplified 杆 covers two readings: gǎn for a stick or shaft and the measure word for guns (笔杆, 一杆枪), and gān for a pole (旗杆, 栏杆). Read it by the word it sits in.
column6: Tā shǒu lǐ wòzhe yī gǎn qiāng.
column7: He held a rifle in his hand.
column9: Read gǎn, 桿 is a stick or shaft and the measure word for guns (筆桿, 一桿槍); a pole read gān is usually written 杆, as in 欄杆.

column3: One generation or era. 新一代 is the new generation of people or products (新一代手机); 年轻一代 and 下一代 are the young and the next generation.
column4: 新一代手机已经上市了。
column5: 新一代手機已經上市了。
column6: Xīn yīdài shǒujī yǐjīng shàngshì le.
column7: The new generation of phones is already on sale.
column9: One generation or era. 新一代 is the new generation of people or products (新一代手機); 年輕一代 and 下一代 are the young and the next generation.

column3: A large batch of people or goods, put before the noun: 大批游客, 大批货物. It does not work as a predicate on its own. 大 is a picture of a person standing facing forward.
column4: 大批游客涌入了这座小城。
column5: 大批遊客湧入了這座小城。
column6: Dàpī yóukè yǒngrù le zhè zuò xiǎochéng.
column7: Large numbers of tourists poured into this small city.
column9: A large batch of people or goods, put before the noun: 大批遊客, 大批貨物. It does not work as a predicate on its own. 大 is a picture of a person standing facing forward.

column3: The vast majority. 绝 adds 'by far' to 大多数 (most), and it is followed by people or parts: 绝大多数人, 绝大部分. One scholar suggests 多 is two pieces of meat 肉: meat was scarce, so two pieces meant a lot.
column4: 绝大多数学生都通过了考试。
column5: 絕大多數學生都通過了考試。
column6: Juédàduōshù xuéshēng dōu tōngguò le kǎoshì.
column7: The vast majority of the students passed the exam.
column9: The vast majority. 絕 adds 'by far' to 大多數 (most), and it is followed by people or parts: 絕大多數人, 絕大部分. One scholar suggests 多 is two pieces of meat 肉: meat was scarce, so two pieces meant a lot.

column3: The total amount of something taken as a whole, in economics and statistics: 能源消费总量, 进口总量, and 总量控制 (capping the total).
column4: 这个城市的用水总量在增加。
column5: 這個城市的用水總量在增加。
column6: Zhège chéngshì de yòngshuǐ zǒngliàng zài zēngjiā.
column7: The total water use of this city is increasing.
column9: The total amount of something taken as a whole, in economics and statistics: 能源消費總量, 進口總量, and 總量控制 (capping the total).

column3: A written way to say 'all sorts of', usually before abstract nouns and without 的: 种种原因, 种种困难, 种种迹象.
column4: 由于种种原因，会议推迟了。
column5: 由於種種原因，會議推遲了。
column6: Yóuyú zhǒngzhǒng yuányīn, huìyì tuīchí le.
column7: For various reasons, the meeting was postponed.
column9: A written way to say 'all sorts of', usually before abstract nouns and without 的: 種種原因, 種種困難, 種種跡象.

column3: The gap between two percentages: from 5% to 7% is two 百分点, not 40%. Common in economic news. 分 shows a knife 刀 separating something (八).
column4: 失业率上升了两个百分点。
column5: 失業率上升了兩個百分點。
column6: Shīyèlǜ shàngshēng le liǎng gè bǎifēndiǎn.
column7: The unemployment rate rose by two percentage points.
column9: The gap between two percentages: from 5% to 7% is two 百分點, not 40%. Common in economic news. 分 shows a knife 刀 separating something (八).

column3: An index for anything rated by number: 股票指数, 物价指数, 空气质量指数, 紫外线指数. In math it is the exponent.
column4: 今天的紫外线指数很高。
column5: 今天的紫外線指數很高。
column6: Jīntiān de zǐwàixiàn zhǐshù hěn gāo.
column7: The UV index is very high today.
column9: An index for anything rated by number: 股票指數, 物價指數, 空氣質量指數, 紫外線指數. In math it is the exponent.

column3: The written and mathematical 'less than' (<), with 大于 for '>'. In ordinary speech you say 比…小 instead.
column4: 年龄小于十八岁的人不能进入。
column5: 年齡小於十八歲的人不能進入。
column6: Niánlíng xiǎoyú shíbā suì de rén bùnéng jìnrù.
column7: People under eighteen may not enter.
column9: The written and mathematical 'less than' (<), with 大於 for '>'. In ordinary speech you say 比…小 instead.

column3: 'In many respects': 在多方面, 多方面的 (many-sided), or before a verb, 多方面努力 (effort on several fronts). 面 began as a picture of a face, with the eye drawn larger.
column4: 这个问题需要从多方面来考虑。
column5: 這個問題需要從多方面來考慮。
column6: Zhège wèntí xūyào cóng duōfāngmiàn lái kǎolǜ.
column7: This question needs to be considered from many angles.
column9: 'In many respects': 在多方面, 多方面的 (many-sided), or before a verb, 多方面努力 (effort on several fronts). 面 began as a picture of a face, with the eye drawn larger.

column3: A surprise that is always pleasant: 给你一个惊喜, and 惊喜 also works as an adjective or a verb. 喜 combines a drum with a mouth.
column4: 生日那天，朋友给了我一个惊喜。
column5: 生日那天，朋友給了我一個驚喜。
column6: Shēngrì nà tiān, péngyou gěi le wǒ yī gè jīngxǐ.
column7: On my birthday, a friend gave me a nice surprise.
column9: A surprise that is always pleasant: 給你一個驚喜, and 驚喜 also works as an adjective or a verb. 驚 has a horse 馬, since horses are easily startled. 喜 combines a drum with a mouth.

column3: Being alone in a deep, lasting way. It describes a person, a life or a feeling: 孤独感, 孤独的生活, 孤独终老 (to die alone).
column4: 他一个人住在山里，过着孤独的生活。
column5: 他一個人住在山裡，過著孤獨的生活。
column6: Tā yī gè rén zhù zài shān lǐ, guòzhe gūdú de shēnghuó.
column7: He lives alone in the mountains, leading a solitary life.
column9: Being alone in a deep, lasting way. It describes a person, a life or a feeling: 孤獨感, 孤獨的生活, 孤獨終老 (to die alone).

column3: Worry about a situation, more formal than 担心 and common in news: 令人担忧 (worrying), 表示担忧 (to voice concern).
column4: 专家对经济前景表示担忧。
column5: 專家對經濟前景表示擔憂。
column6: Zhuānjiā duì jīngjì qiánjǐng biǎoshì dānyōu.
column7: Experts voiced concern about the economic outlook.
column9: Worry about a situation, more formal than 擔心 and common in news: 令人擔憂 (worrying), 表示擔憂 (to voice concern).

column3: For fates, lives and scenes that are tragic, not for a passing sad mood: 悲惨的命运, 悲惨的遭遇, 场面悲惨.
column4: 这部电影讲了一个悲惨的故事。
column5: 這部電影講了一個悲慘的故事。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng le yī gè bēicǎn de gùshi.
column7: This film tells a tragic story.
column9: For fates, lives and scenes that are tragic, not for a passing sad mood: 悲慘的命運, 悲慘的遭遇, 場面悲慘.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 发了怒, 发什么怒. 发 here means to let out a feeling, as in 发火, 发脾气, 发愁.
column6: Lǎobǎn yī tīng jiù fānù le.
column7: The boss flew into a rage as soon as he heard.
